Random and home configurations

Source: R/robot-model.R
robot_configurations.Rd

robot_random_configuration() samples uniformly within the position limits; unbounded joints are sampled in \([-\pi, \pi)\) (revolute and continuous) or \([-1, 1]\) meters (prismatic). The caller's random number state is left unchanged when seed is supplied. robot_home() returns zeros projected onto the limits.

Usage

robot_random_configuration(robot, n = 1, seed = NULL)

robot_home(robot)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model.

n

Number of configurations.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A vector (n = 1) or a matrix with one row per configuration.

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar2")
robot_random_configuration(robot, 3, seed = 1)
#>          joint1     joint2
#> [1,] -1.4733525 -0.8034692
#> [2,]  0.4577512  2.5648452
#> [3,] -1.8743877  2.5031562
